beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about a one-character bug in our regulatory intelligence pipeline that meant a single urgent filing, the exact case our alert system exists for, could silently generate no alert at all.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: fellow's name + one-line summary of what the video covers, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: Our alert email only fires when there's something urgent to report. This week, I found the one case it was never built to handle: exactly one urgent item. Not zero. Not two. One.
beats.new_visual_element: A counter showing 0, 1 (highlighted/flagged), 2, with 1 visually distinct from the other two

shot.note: Real framing of the exact-1-item edge case, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real line, straight from the workflow. The alert node only builds an email if there's more than one new high-priority item. newItems.length greater than 1. Greater than, not greater than or equal. A single critical filing doesn't clear that bar.
beats.new_visual_element: The real verbatim line of code shown large, newItems.length > 1, with the 1 visually flagged

shot.note: [Source: B6-VERIFICATION.md] Verbatim code line, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: I traced where a failed check actually goes, it lands on an empty branch with nowhere to go. No error, no log line, nothing a person would notice. Just an alert that never arrives. The fix is one character: greater than one becomes greater than zero.
beats.new_visual_element: Before/after diff, > 1 struck through, > 0 added, with an arrow showing the failed branch's dead end

shot.note: [Source: B6-VERIFICATION.md] Real diff, matches the committed fix exactly (f9eed1e).

beats.narration_text: Before trusting the fix, I ran the real extracted code, not a rewritten copy, against zero, one, and two items, before and after. Zero stayed correctly silent. One went from silently skipped to a real email. Two already worked, and still does. Then I re-ran it against the actual patched file on disk, to confirm the real change behaves the same way.
beats.new_visual_element: The real 3-row before/after table (0/1/2 items), with the 1-item row visually highlighted as the one that changed

shot.note: [Source: B6-VERIFICATION.md verification table] Real measured harness results, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Two honest limits. First: this wasn't caught by a live incident, it was caught by re-reading the code, I don't have evidence this specific case ever occurred on a real run. Second: while tracing this, I found a related but separate compatibility gap, a downstream service's source list doesn't yet account for a newer classification change, flagged for a future week, not fixed yet.
beats.new_visual_element: 2 honest-limit cards, side by side, full weight, no softening language

shot.note: [Source: FACTCHECK.md #5, #6] Full weight, not softened, per established house discipline.

beats.narration_text: An alert system is only as good as the cases it was actually built to handle. The scariest bugs aren't the ones that crash, they're the ones that quietly do nothing at all.
